terms.meaning: The period of change from childhood to adulthood, generally from about 10 to 19 years of age.
The stage when the body of a child changes into an adult body capable of reproduction.
Features that help to tell males from females but are not directly involved in reproduction.
Chemicals made in the body that control the changes of adolescence.
The discharge of blood in the menstrual cycle, a natural sign of health in adolescent girls and women.
Pimples on the skin, when oily secretions block the pores and bacteria grow.
Harassing someone online, such as by spreading false rumours or sharing their photos without consent.

items.name: Growth spurt
items.formula: Height and weight increase quickly in both boys and girls.
items.example: A student may grow out of a uniform in a single year.

items.name: Voice and Adam’s apple
items.formula: In boys the voice box grows and may show as a bump, and the voice deepens. In girls it grows less.
items.example: A boy’s voice may crack for a while.

items.name: Body hair
items.formula: Hair appears in the armpits and pubic region in both. Boys also get facial hair.
items.example: A moustache is a secondary sexual characteristic.

items.name: Menstrual cycle
items.formula: Generally repeats every 28 to 30 days. Bleeding lasts about 3 to 7 days.
items.example: It begins at puberty and generally ends by the age of 45 to 55 years.

items.name: Emotional changes
items.formula: Mood swings, strong feelings and curiosity are normal.
items.example: Music, sport and helping others are good outlets.

items.name: Food for strong bones
items.formula: Calcium and protein from milk, curd, paneer and millets.
items.example: A glass of milk helps bones to grow.

items.name: Food for healthy blood
items.formula: Iron from spinach, beans and dried fruits such as raisins.
items.example: Too little iron can cause anaemia.

items.name: Dorothy Hodgkin
items.formula: Won the 1964 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for finding the structure of vitamin B12.
items.example: We must get this vitamin from food.

items.name: Personal hygiene
items.formula: Wash daily, use clean pads, and wrap used pads in paper before putting them in a dustbin.
items.example: Biodegradable pads are kinder to the environment.

items.name: Addictive substances
items.formula: Say NO to tobacco, gutka, alcohol and drugs, which harm body and mind.
items.example: Friends pressing you to try is not a good enough reason.

items.name: Exercise and yoga
items.formula: Regular activity keeps adolescents healthy. International Yoga Day is 21 June.
items.example: Sport, walking or yoga every day.

items.name: Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram
items.formula: A national programme for adolescent health, using peer education.
items.example: Young people learn health facts from each other.

items.name: Menstrual Hygiene Scheme
items.formula: Gives pads free or at low prices to adolescent girls in rural areas, with awareness programmes.
items.example: It is a Government of India scheme.

items.name: Suvidha
items.formula: Low-cost biodegradable pads sold through Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
items.example: A girl can buy them at a Jan Aushadhi shop.

items.name: Shuchi scheme
items.formula: Karnataka gives free pads to girls in government schools.

items.name: Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan
items.formula: A campaign against substance abuse. De-addiction helpline: 14446.
items.example: Anyone who needs help can call the number.

mistakes.text: Secondary sexual characteristics are not directly involved in reproduction, even though they appear at puberty.
Menstruation is natural. Keeping girls apart during it has no scientific basis.
Adolescence and puberty are not the same word: adolescence is the whole 10 to 19 period, and puberty is the change towards being able to reproduce.
